title: Corn Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Corn Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Corn nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in mais, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Corn nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your mais (corn) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, zinc, sulfur, magnesium, calcium, boron, copper and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Maize leaf yellowing in a broad band along the midrib while the edges stay green, from nitrogen shortage
heroImage.credit: Vishnu Khade, Maize Nutrient Deficiency Dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, sulfur, calcium, boron, copper and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which corn nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Corn nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of mais
rows: old, lower leaves, the whole plant
Lower leaves turn yellow in a V from the tip down the midrib, and plants are pale and thin.
old, lower leaves, the whole plant
Young plants are short and dark green, with purple red edges on the lower leaves.
old, lower leaves, leaf edges and tips
Lower leaves dry brown along the edges while the middle stays green, and stalks break and fall.
old, lower leaves, between the veins
Lower leaves get yellow to white stripes between the veins, later turning reddish purple.

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of mais

Wide white or pale yellow bands on both sides of the midrib from the leaf base, on short plants with bunched leaves.
young leaves and the tip, the whole plant
The young upper leaves are the palest, while the lower leaves stay greener.

Tips of the young leaves stick together like a ladder, on very acid soil.
Upper leaves have white spots and waxy brown streaks, and tassels and ears fail to come out.
The youngest leaves come out yellow, and their tips brown, roll and break.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a corn nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest corn nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Maize leaf yellowing in a broad band along the midrib while the edges stay green, from nitrogen shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Vishnu Khade, Maize Nutrient Deficiency Dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: The lowest leaves turn pale, then yellow in a V shape that starts at the leaf tip and runs down the midrib. The yellowing climbs the plant if nothing is done, and the old leaves dry from the tip. Stalks stay thin and plants short, and ears come out small with poorly filled tips. You see it most at this stage: knee high to silking. The crop takes up the most nitrogen in the month before tasseling.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. Lower leaves turn yellow in a V from the tip, and ears come out small with bare tips.
In white or glutinous corn, it looks much the same. Lower leaves turn yellow in a V from the tip down the midrib, and plants are pale and thin.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in mais
Too little fertilizer, nitrogen washed out by heavy rain or irrigation, nitrogen lost from dry or hard soil, sandy soil. Fields flooded in hot weather.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency also yellows the plant but starts on the young upper leaves. Potassium deficiency browns the leaf edges, not the midrib. To be sure, check that the yellowing started on the bottom leaves, in a V along the midrib. Compare with a few rows given extra urea, and have the soil tested before the next planting.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Sidedress Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 beside the row and cover it with soil, then irrigate or wait for rain. Follow the soil test for the rate. For quick help, give a 1 percent urea spray (10 g per liter) twice, 15 days apart. Nitrogen given after the ears start filling helps much less.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, test the soil before planting, split nitrogen between planting and knee high, and avoid packing the soil hard.
Phosphorus deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Young corn seedling with deep purple leaves from phosphorus shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Mary Ann Hansen, Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University, CC BY 3.0 US, via ipmimages.org

blocks.text: Young plants grow slowly and stay small and thin, with dark green leaves. The edges and tips of the older leaves turn reddish purple. The color can spread over the whole blade, while new leaves stay green. Later the crop matures late and ears are small, twisted or poorly formed. You see it most at this stage: seedling to knee high. The purple usually fades once plants pass about 1 meter, but the yield loss stays.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. Young plants are short and dark green, with purple red edges on the lower leaves.
In white or glutinous corn, it looks much the same. Young plants are short and dark green, with purple red edges on the lower leaves.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in mais
Acid soils and very alkaline soils that hold phosphorus tightly, cold wet soil, hard packed soil. Roots hurt by insects or fertilizer.
How to tell it apart

Some hybrids show purple leaves when young even with enough phosphorus, so compare with other plants and the soil test. Magnesium deficiency also gives purple tints, but with yellow stripes between the veins. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus before planting. A real shortage shows on many plants in the same soil patch, not on one hybrid only.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Phosphorus works best at planting. For the standing crop, give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter). For the next crop, put 16 20 0, Complete 14 14 14 or DAP in the furrow at planting, following the soil test.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, band phosphorus near the seed at planting, and lime very acid soils as the soil test advises.
Potassium deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Corn plant whose lower leaves are yellow then brown along the edges from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Alandmanson, CC BY SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: The edges and tips of the lower leaves turn yellow, then brown and dry, while the middle of the leaf stays green. It moves up the plant if the shortage goes on. Stalks get weak and plants fall over late in the season, and ears are small and pointed with empty tips. You see it most at this stage: shows about 4 to 6 weeks after planting (around the 6 leaf stage) and again at grain filling.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. Lower leaf edges dry brown, and ears are short and pointed with unfilled tips.
In white or glutinous corn, it looks much the same. Lower leaves dry brown along the edges while the middle stays green, and stalks break and fall.
Why potassium deficiency happens in mais
Sandy soils, highly weathered acid soils, hard, dry or waterlogged soils that limit roots. Fields where earlier crops took away a lot of potassium.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen yellowing runs down the midrib in a V, while potassium burns the leaf edges. Drought scorch hits many leaves at once. To be sure, soil test for potassium, and look for brown edges starting on the bottom leaves. A leaf tissue test of the ear leaf confirms it.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Sidedress Muriate of potash 0 0 60 beside the row early, following the soil test. Give a 1 percent potassium chloride or potassium sulfate spray (10 g per liter) twice, 15 days apart.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, return stalks and leaves to the field, and give potash at planting when the soil test is low.
Zinc deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Young corn plant with broad white to pale yellow bands on the young leaves from zinc shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Agronom, CC BY SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Pale yellow to white bands appear between the veins, starting at the base of the leaf and running toward the tip. While the edges, tip and midrib stay green. Internodes stay short, so plants look stunted with bunched leaves. In severe cases the new leaves come out almost white (white bud), and leaf edges and stems turn reddish. You see it most at this stage: seedling to knee high. Plants often outgrow mild cases.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. Wide white or pale yellow bands on both sides of the midrib from the leaf base, on short plants with bunched leaves.
In white or glutinous corn, it looks much the same. Wide white or pale yellow bands on both sides of the midrib from the leaf base, on short plants with bunched leaves.
Why zinc deficiency happens in mais
High pH soils (pH 7.5 and up), low organic matter, cool wet soil. Heavy phosphorus on soils already low in zinc.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency stripes the old leaves, not a band at the base of young leaves. Iron deficiency stripes the full length of the young leaf. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray 0.5 percent Zinc sulfate (5 g per liter) twice, 15 days apart. For the soil, give 20 to 25 kg zinc sulfate per hectare. The University of Kentucky bands about 19 kg zinc sulfate per hectare (17 pounds per acre) near the row.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, on high pH or zinc poor soils, add zinc sulfate to the basal fertilizer.
Sulfur deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Young corn plant with pale yellow leaves all over, newest leaves palest, from sulfur shortage (small credit line in corner)
blocks.caption: Photo: Soil Science, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: The whole plant looks pale like nitrogen deficiency. But the young upper leaves are the palest, and up close they show faint yellow stripes between the veins. Plants stay short and upright, and maturity comes late. You see it most at this stage: early growth. It may fade as roots go deeper and the soil warms.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. The young upper leaves are the palest, while the lower leaves stay greener.
In white or glutinous corn, it looks much the same. The young upper leaves are the palest, while the lower leaves stay greener.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in mais
Acid sandy soils, low organic matter, waterlogged soils, and heavy rain soon after planting. Years of urea and other sulfur free fertilizers make it more likely.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency starts on the old lower leaves. Zinc deficiency gives a white band at the leaf base. To be sure, note which leaves yellowed first, then test soil and leaves for sulfur.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Use Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 for the next nitrogen sidedress, and place a sulfur bearing fertilizer near the row. Follow the soil test for the rate.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include ammonium sulfate or another sulfur source in the program on sandy or low organic matter soils.
Magnesium deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Corn leaf with pale yellow stripes between green veins from magnesium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Alandmanson, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Yellow to white stripes appear between the veins of the lower leaves, sometimes with small dead spots that look like a string of beads. Later the old leaves take on a reddish purple color and can die back at the tips and margins. Growth stays normal unless it is severe. You see it most at this stage: early growth to the middle of the season.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. Lower leaves get yellow to white stripes between the veins, later turning reddish purple.
In white or glutinous corn, it looks much the same. Lower leaves get yellow to white stripes between the veins, later turning reddish purple.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in mais
Very acid, sandy soils in rainy areas, fields that were never limed, and heavy potash on soils already low in magnesium.
How to tell it apart
Iron and manganese deficiency give similar stripes but on the young leaves. Zinc gives a band near the base of young leaves. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
Apply magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) to the soil or as a leaf spray. Give a 2 percent spray (20 g per liter). On acid soils use Dolomite following the soil test.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid fields with dolomite, and do not overdo potash.
Calcium deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Maize whorl whose newest leaves have torn, ragged brown edges and cling together from calcium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Devechio et al., Journal of Agricultural Science 2022, CC BY 4.0, via CCSE

blocks.text: The tips of new leaves stick to the leaf below, so the whorl looks like a ladder or a row of hooks. Young leaves are light green with whitish streaks and brittle, brown, sticky edges. Plants can be badly stunted. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. Tips of the young leaves stick together like a ladder, on very acid soil.
Why calcium deficiency happens in mais
Rare. It needs very acid soils (below pH 5), unlimed weathered uplands, or soils where magnesium and potassium crowd out calcium.
How to tell it apart
Boron deficiency also hurts the growing tip but gives white spots and short upper internodes. Acid soil damage from aluminum stunts the roots. To be sure, soil pH and calcium test.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
Apply Agricultural lime or Dolomite following the soil test. One extremely acid farm in Isabela needed 3.6 tons of lime per hectare. Gypsum adds calcium without raising the pH.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid uplands before planting, ahead of the rains.
Boron deficiency in corn

Young leaves get small white or yellow spots and raised, waxy brown streaks, and turn brittle. Upper internodes stay short. Tassels and ear shoots are small and may not come out, so few kernels set. You see it most at this stage: before tasseling up to silking.
In sweet corn, it looks much the same. Upper leaves have white spots and waxy brown streaks, and tassels and ears fail to come out.
In white or glutinous corn, it looks much the same. Upper leaves have white spots and waxy brown streaks, and tassels and ears fail to come out.
Why boron deficiency happens in mais
Rare. Sandy soils low in organic matter, high pH soils and drought.
How to tell it apart
Drought also delays ear shoots and spoils pollination, so both can happen together. Zinc gives bands, not spots. To be sure, test leaves and soil for boron before treating.
What to apply for boron deficiency
Give a 0.5 percent borax spray (5 g per liter) every 15 days. Corn is very sensitive to too much boron. So never go above the advised rate and do not put boron in the seed row.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up, and irrigate at tasseling during dry spells.
Copper deficiency in corn

New leaves already look yellow when they unroll from the whorl, then their tips brown, curl and snap off. Striping much like an iron shortage can show, the stalk goes soft and floppy, and older leaves may die along their margins. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why copper deficiency happens in mais
Rare. Seen on peat and other high organic matter soils and soils above pH 7.5.
How to tell it apart
Iron deficiency gives similar streaks. Nitrogen plus sulfur shortage in cool weather can look like mild copper deficiency. To be sure, soil and leaf test for copper.
What to apply for copper deficiency
Give a 0.2 percent copper sulfate spray (2 g per liter). About 1 kg of copper per hectare was needed on one Cagayan soil, so follow the soil test.

Sold here with copper: **Omex Zynergy** by Jardine Distribution, Inc. (3.75 percent zinc and 2.11 percent copper), **Grower's Choice Copper Sulphate Pentahydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (25 percent copper and 12 percent sulfur), **Agsmart Copper Sulphate** by AgSmart Corporation (25 percent copper and 12 percent sulfur) and **Liquid Chelate Copper w/ Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent copper and 2 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [copper deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/copper-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test for copper before planting on peat or alkaline soils.
Iron deficiency in corn

blocks.alt: Young maize leaves striped pale yellow between green veins along their whole length from iron shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Alves et al., Plants (MDPI) 2026, CC BY 4.0, via the publisher

blocks.text: Long pale green to nearly white stripes run between the veins of the upper leaves, while the veins stay green. As it worsens the veins pale too, the crop looks bleached, and plants are stunted. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth.
Why iron deficiency happens in mais
Rare in corn. Only on high pH, calcareous soils, worse when the soil is cold, wet and poorly aerated.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium also stripes leaves, but the old ones. Zinc gives a band at the base of the leaf, not stripes the full length. To be sure, soil pH test (calcareous soil is the warning sign) and a leaf test.
What to apply for iron deficiency
Give 20 to 25 kg ferrous sulfate per hectare to the soil, or a 1 percent ferrous sulfate spray (10 g per liter) every week until new leaves come out green.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add manure and use an acid forming fertilizer such as ammonium sulfate on calcareous soil.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any corn nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your mais needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Corn nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my mais leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves turn yellow in a V from the tip down the midrib, and plants are pale and thin. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in corn?
items.a: Sidedress Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 beside the row and cover it with soil, then irrigate or wait for rain. Follow the soil test for the rate.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in corn?
items.a: Phosphorus works best at planting. For the standing crop, give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in corn?
items.a: Sidedress Muriate of potash 0 0 60 beside the row early, following the soil test. Give a 1 percent potassium chloride or potassium sulfate spray (10 g per liter) twice, 15 days apart.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my mais lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the corn nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
